problem:
Harbour Energy, a utility creditor, collects monthly bills from 40,000 household customers by SEPA Direct Debit. Its billing system generates a collection file each month, but the mandate data behind the file is uneven: some mandates were signed on paper years ago and their scanned images are stored in a shared drive, some were created online and their consent evidence is in a different system, and some mandates were amended when customers changed bank accounts, with the amendment recorded only as a free-text note. When a collection is rejected for a missing or invalid mandate, the billing team cannot prove quickly whether a valid mandate existed, and the customer disputes the collection.

The lifecycle problem is wider than storage. A mandate that has not been used for 36 months must not be used, yet Harbour Energy has no systematic check for dormant mandates, so a customer who left three years ago could still be collected from if their account were still open. Amendments are not versioned, so when a customer changes account, the old account details and the new ones sit side by side with no clear current version. Cancellations arrive by phone, email and letter, and not all of them reach the mandate register, so a cancelled mandate can still generate a collection.

Harbour Energy needs a mandate lifecycle that covers creation, amendment, cancellation, reference and evidence, with each mandate carrying a unique reference, a status, a version history and retrievable consent evidence, and with collection validation that checks the mandate before any file is submitted. The creditor, not the debtor's bank, owns the mandate evidence, and the bank must be able to rely on the creditor's validation.
solution:
Create a single mandate register as the system of record. Every mandate gets a unique mandate reference, the creditor identifier, the debtor name and IBAN, the scheme, the date of signature, the signature or consent evidence, the status, and a version number. Amendments create a new version rather than overwriting the old one, so the history shows what changed, when, and under whose authority. Cancellations change the status to cancelled with a date, reason and channel, and a cancelled mandate can never generate a collection again. Evidence must be retrievable by reference within the agreed service level, whether the original was paper or electronic.

Build collection validation against the register, not against the billing file alone. Before a collection is included in the submission file, the platform checks that an active mandate exists for the debtor, that the creditor identifier and debtor account match the current mandate version, that the mandate has been used within the last 36 months, and that the pre-notification requirement has been met. Any collection that fails is routed to repair or rejection with a clear reason, and never submitted in the hope that the debtor's bank will accept it.

Finally, govern the lifecycle with controls and reporting. Report monthly on dormant mandates approaching 36 months, on mandates whose evidence cannot be retrieved, on amendments and cancellations by channel, and on collections rejected for mandate reasons. Make the mandate owner accountable for evidence completeness, and test the register with a simulated dispute: can the team produce the mandate, its version history and its evidence for any given collection within the agreed time?

decision.question: You are the business analyst for Harbour Energy. A collection is rejected for a missing mandate, but the billing team believes a mandate was signed. Dormant mandates are not checked, amendments are unversioned, and cancellations sometimes never reach the mandate register. The operations director asks for your recommendation.

options.label: A
options.detail: Collect from every customer and refund anyone who complains.

options.label: B
options.detail: Build a governed mandate lifecycle with a unique reference, status, versioned amendments, retrievable consent evidence and a 36-month dormancy rule, and validate every collection against the mandate before submission.

options.label: C
options.detail: Resubmit the collection and ask the debtor's bank to check the mandate.

options.label: D
options.detail: Delete all mandates older than a year to remove the stale data.

decisionRationale: Option B is correct because it fixes the lifecycle itself: unique references, versioned amendments, evidence retention and dormancy control, with validation before submission so invalid collections never leave the creditor. Option C shifts the creditor's responsibility to the debtor's bank. Option A collects without authority and creates refund and complaint volumes. Option D destroys valid mandates and their evidence.

steps.title: Signs the mandate, on paper or electronically, authorising Harbour Energy to collect by direct debit
Registers the mandate with a unique reference, creditor identifier, debtor IBAN and retrievable consent evidence
Amends the mandate, for example by changing bank account, creating a new versioned record
Generates the monthly collection and checks each item against the current mandate version
Validates the mandate and submits the collection file
Routes the collection to the debtor PSP
Debits the debtor account on the due date
Reconciles the collection against the mandate register and the billing record

happy: A customer signs a mandate that is registered with a unique reference and retrievable evidence. Monthly collections are validated against the current mandate version, pass, and are submitted and debited on the due date. An amendment creates a new version and later collections use the new account. A cancellation stops future collections immediately. Every collection can be traced to its mandate and evidence.

negative.title: Mandate missing or invalid
negative.detail: A collection is generated for a debtor with no active mandate, or with mandate details that do not match the collection. Block the collection before submission, route it to repair with a clear reason, and do not submit it in the hope the debtor PSP will accept it.

negative.title: Mandate revoked after file creation
negative.detail: The customer cancels the mandate after the collection file has been generated but before submission. Re-check mandate status at submission time, exclude the revoked item from the file, and record the exclusion with its reason.

negative.title: Dormant mandate over 36 months
negative.detail: A mandate has not been used for 36 months and a collection is attempted. Block the collection, mark the mandate dormant, and require a new mandate from the customer before any further collection.

negative.title: Evidence unavailable in a dispute
negative.detail: A customer disputes a collection and the signed mandate cannot be retrieved. Treat the mandate as unproven, refund or reverse under the applicable process, escalate the evidence gap to the mandate owner, and fix the storage failure.

negative.title: Duplicate mandate reference
negative.detail: Two mandates carry the same reference for different debtors. Reject the duplicate at registration, enforce uniqueness in the register, and investigate the source system that generated it.

technical: Model the mandate as a versioned entity with a unique reference, creditor identifier, debtor IBAN, scheme, signature date, evidence pointer, status and version number, and never overwrite a prior version. Enforce referential integrity so a collection must reference an existing active mandate version. Apply the 36-month dormancy rule as a scheduled check that flags and then blocks dormant mandates. Store consent evidence with a durable pointer and a retrieval service level, and retain it for the period the scheme and local rules require. Use correlation IDs to link the mandate, the collection instruction, the interbank message and the ledger entry. Log every lifecycle event, creation, amendment, cancellation and use, with actor, timestamp and reason.

accounting: Each collected item produces a credit to Harbour Energy and a debit to the debtor, with the batch control total reconciled against executed, rejected and returned items. A collection that is blocked for a mandate reason never posts, so it appears in the exception report rather than in the ledger. Returns and refunds are posted as separate linked events against the original collection, never by deleting it. Operations works from a mandate exception worklist with SLA targets for evidence retrieval and repair, and Finance monitors the value of collections blocked for mandate reasons as a measure of billing quality. Dormant mandates are reported monthly so the business can see how much of its mandate base is no longer usable.
